reference.source: DeVita, Hellman and Rosenberg's Cancer / NCCN genetic/familial guidelines
clinicalPearls: Caused by germline variants in the succinate dehydrogenase complex genes (SDHB, SDHD, SDHC, SDHA and SDHAF2), inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern, with SDHD and SDHAF2 showing a striking parent-of-origin (paternal transmission) effect
Produces phaeochromocytomas of the adrenal medulla and paragangliomas at head-and-neck and sympathetic sites, which may be multifocal
SDHB variants carry the highest risk of malignant, metastatic and extra-adrenal disease, whereas SDHD variants often cause multiple head-and-neck paragangliomas
Catecholamine-secreting tumours cause paroxysmal hypertension, palpitations, headache and sweating, while many head-and-neck paragangliomas are non-secretory and present as painless masses
Loss of SDHB expression on tumour immunohistochemistry is a reliable clue to an underlying SDHx defect and directs germline testing
The complex also predisposes to gastrointestinal stromal tumours and renal cell carcinoma, so surveillance extends beyond the classic tumours
Biochemical screening with plasma or urinary metanephrines and periodic whole-body imaging form the basis of surveillance
reference.pathophysiology: Succinate dehydrogenase is a mitochondrial enzyme complex that participates in both the tricarboxylic acid cycle and the electron transport chain. Germline loss-of-function variants, followed by somatic loss of the remaining allele, inactivate the complex and cause intracellular succinate to accumulate. Excess succinate inhibits oxygen-sensing prolyl hydroxylases and stabilises hypoxia-inducible factors, generating a pseudohypoxic state that promotes angiogenesis and proliferation, and also alters DNA and histone methylation, together driving the development of paragangliomas and related tumours.
additionalDifferentials: Carney triad (non-hereditary gastric GIST, paraganglioma and pulmonary chondroma)
additionalInvestigations: Germline sequencing and deletion/duplication analysis of the SDHx genes within a phaeochromocytoma-paraganglioma panel
Plasma free or 24-hour urinary metanephrines and normetanephrines
Whole-body MRI or functional imaging to localise and stage multifocal tumours
Tumour SDHB immunohistochemistry to support a succinate dehydrogenase defect
Cross-sectional abdominal imaging for renal cell carcinoma and gastrointestinal stromal tumours
Audiological and head-and-neck assessment for glomus tumours
redFlags: Paroxysmal hypertension with headache, palpitations and sweating indicating catecholamine excess
A hypertensive crisis, particularly if precipitated by anaesthesia or an unblocked procedure
A rapidly enlarging or metastatic tumour, especially in SDHB carriers
A pulsatile neck mass with cranial nerve dysfunction from a head-and-neck paraganglioma
reference.prognosis: Prognosis depends strongly on genotype and tumour behaviour: many head-and-neck paragangliomas are indolent, whereas SDHB-related disease has a higher malignant potential and worse outcome. Lifelong biochemical and imaging surveillance enables early detection, and appropriate preoperative adrenergic blockade before surgery is critical to safe management.
pitfalls: Proceeding to surgery or anaesthesia without adequate preoperative alpha-adrenergic blockade in secretory tumours
Assuming head-and-neck paragangliomas are non-functional without biochemical confirmation
Overlooking the parent-of-origin effect and misjudging risk in SDHD and SDHAF2 families
Neglecting surveillance for associated renal cell carcinoma and gastrointestinal stromal tumours
references: DeVita, Hellman and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles and Practice of Oncology
